name: POST /api/sla/alerts/dispatch - Retry undelivered SLA notifications
description: Re-attempts the outbound notification for every SLA alert still in the pending state, oldest first. A command that changes state without creating an addressable resource, so it answers 200 (MUST-54). This endpoint exists because the alert ROW is written before the notification is sent: the escalation is durable and visible in-app the moment it is raised, and the outbound send through ProjexCloud sdk-notification is a separate, retryable step. A gateway outage therefore degrades the CHANNEL rather than silencing the escalation, and this sweep drains the backlog once the gateway returns - which is exactly the guarantee a manager escalation needs. Each attempt uses the alert id as the idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout cannot deliver the same notification twice upstream. An alert that has exhausted its retry budget (attempts at or above the maximum) moves to failed and is skipped by later runs so a permanently undeliverable address cannot stall the queue; the row stays readable in-app. When the gateway is UNCONFIGURED the sweep is a deliberate no-op that leaves alerts pending rather than marking them delivered - claiming delivery no notification service ever saw would be a lie the audit trail could not detect. limit is clamped to 1..500 and defaults to 100. EXPECT attempted:0 IN A CLEAN QA RUN and that is the CORRECT contract - alerts are only raised for a lead that is at_risk or breached, and no API can make a response clock expire. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: Reject a limit above the maximum

errorCases.when: limit is present and not an integer between 1 and 500
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
